answer: Repeated route fingerprinting requires each identity to route a random challenge through an inlet and return signed arrival times. The coordinator injects a zephyr of low-rate challenges and compares timing fingerprints across identities. Duplicates sharing hardware or network egress produce a correlated signal above threshold, so all linked identities are suspended. An attacker must therefore pay separate hardware, egress, and a recurring two-unit ledger rent per identity.
